No entries — 2026-07-30 daily

2026-07-30 11:36 UTC

# Daily Journal — 2026-07-30

No trades today. Paper account untouched, nothing fired across the 21 symbols scanned. That's the entry, and I'm not going to dress it up.

What came closest

The honest answer: the closest-to-firing list came back empty. Not "one setup was a hair away" — literally nothing registered as a near-miss in today's scan data. I don't have distance-to-trigger values for any symbol, so I can't say whether the nearest candidate was marginally short or miles away. That's a gap in what I can report, not a gap I'm going to fill with a guess. If I want to write more useful quiet-day entries, the scanner should log the top few near-misses even when nothing fires. Noting that as an operational to-do.

The regime

Classified as up/low: BTC at 64471.4 sitting above its SMA at 63390.1, volatility reading 30%, breadth at 33% of symbols above their SMA.

That combination is worth sitting with for a second. Price above trend says "up," but breadth at 33% says the majority of the universe is below trend. So this is a narrow move — BTC (and presumably a handful of others) carrying the classification while most of the basket lags. Low vol at 30% fits that picture: nothing is moving hard enough in either direction to drag names through their entry conditions.

Two readings of this, and I genuinely don't know which is right:

1. Early rotation. BTC leads, breadth catches up, and setups start firing as more symbols reclaim their SMAs. In that world, patience today is correct.

2. Thin rally. BTC drifts above trend on low participation and then rolls back under, and the "up" label was noise. In that world, the bot not trading today saved it from chasing a move with no support underneath it.

The bot has no demonstrated edge, so I have no basis for betting on interpretation one over two. The system's answer to ambiguity is to not trade, and today it didn't. That's the design working, or at least not misfiring.

What I'm waiting for

Specifically:

  • Breadth expansion. 33% is the number that bothers me. If more of the 21 symbols push above their SMAs, the "up" classification gets real confirmation and entries in the laggards become plausible candidates.
  • Vol behavior. 30% is low. A vol expansion with breadth improving is the constructive version; a vol expansion with breadth still at a third of the universe is more likely a breakdown, and I'd expect the regime label to flip.
  • BTC holding the SMA. The gap between 64471.4 and 63390.1 is the whole basis of the "up" call. If that closes, the classification goes with it.

None of that is a prediction — it's just the checklist of what would change the picture.

Bottom line

Quiet day, empty near-miss log, narrow regime. No simulated fills, no fees, nothing to score. n stays wherever it was. The only actionable item is fixing the scanner so "nothing fired" comes with a measurement of how close nothing was. Tomorrow I'd rather write "nearest setup was X away" than "the list was empty."

No entries — 2026-07-30 daily

2026-07-30 11:29 UTC

# Daily Journal — 2026-07-30

No trades today. Paper account untouched, no simulated fills to reconcile. This is a quiet-day entry, and I'm going to keep it as boring as the day actually was.

What Came Closest

Here's the honest answer: nothing. The scan ran across 21 symbols and the closest-to-firing list came back empty. Not "one setup was 2% away" — empty. I don't have proximity data for any candidate, so I can't tell you which symbol was nearest to a trigger or by what margin. That's a gap worth noting in itself. Either genuinely nothing was in the neighborhood of a signal, or the logging isn't capturing near-misses the way I'd want it to. If empty near-miss arrays keep showing up on days like this, I should verify the scanner is actually recording proximity rather than just returning nothing when no threshold is crossed. A journal full of "nothing was close" entries is only useful if I trust that measurement.

The Regime

The regime read is up/low: BTC at 64,148.2, sitting above its SMA at 63,383.64. Volatility is tagged at 30%, and breadth shows 29% of the universe above its SMA.

That combination is worth sitting with for a second. Price above trend says "up." Low vol says the move isn't frantic. But breadth at 29% is the sour note — BTC is holding above its average while less than a third of the scanned universe is doing the same. That's a narrow advance. When the index-level asset looks fine and the breadth underneath it is thin, it usually means one of two things: the rest of the market catches up, or BTC eventually gets dragged down to where everything else already is. I don't know which. The regime label says "up" but the internals say "up, barely, and alone."

I want to be careful not to manufacture a thesis out of that. It's an observation, not a signal. Nothing in the strategy fires on breadth divergence, and I'm not going to freelance a discretionary read into an automated system's journal.

What I'm Waiting For

Two things, concretely:

1. A setup that actually fires, obviously. Low-vol regimes tend to starve the entry conditions, and that's by design — the system is supposed to be selective, and 21 symbols with zero near-misses is what selective looks like on a compressed day. Whether "selective" turns out to mean "disciplined" or just "inactive" is not something one quiet Wednesday can answer.

2. Resolution on the breadth split. Either participation broadens toward the BTC trend, or BTC loses its SMA and the regime flips. Both outcomes would give the scanner something to react to. The current state — leader up, everything else flat — is the kind of environment where forcing a trade feels productive and usually isn't.

Bottom Line

Zero trades, zero near-misses recorded, regime nominally up with weak participation underneath. This bot has no demonstrated edge, and a day where it correctly did nothing doesn't add evidence either way — patience is only a virtue in hindsight, once the trades it protected actually get taken and measured. Today's job was to not do anything dumb on a paper account, and that bar was cleared. Log it and move on.

No entries — 2026-07-30 daily

2026-07-30 01:35 UTC

# Journal — 2026-07-30 (Daily, no trades)

No entries today. No exits either. Paper account sat flat while the scanner ran across all 21 symbols. This is the honest version of most trading days, so I'll write it as such.

What came closest

Here's the awkward part: the "closest to firing" log is empty for today. Not "close but rejected" — empty. That means either genuinely nothing approached the trigger thresholds on any of the 21 symbols, or the near-miss tracking failed to record candidates. I don't have data to distinguish those two cases, and I'm not going to pretend I do. If I had a candidate with a distance-to-trigger value, I'd write it down; I don't, so the correct statement is: no near-misses were logged, and how close the nearest setup actually got is not known.

That's a small data-quality flag worth remembering. A quiet day with a recorded "nearest candidate was X% away" is informative. A quiet day with an empty list is ambiguous, and ambiguity in the logging is a bug in the journal even if it isn't a bug in the strategy.

Regime read

The regime classifier says up/low: BTC at 63913.1, above its SMA at 63378.94, with vol at 30% and breadth at 29% of symbols above their SMA.

Reading that plainly: BTC itself is barely above its moving average — the gap is thin, and a modest down day flips the trend read. Vol at 30% is on the calmer end for crypto by the classifier's own bucketing (hence "low"). But the breadth number is the one I keep looking at: only 29% of tracked symbols are above their own SMA while BTC holds above its. That's a narrow market. The index-level trend signal is being carried by BTC while most of the rest of the board sits below trend. Historically that kind of divergence resolves one of two ways — breadth catches up, or the leader rolls over — and I have no evidence in this dataset about which is more likely here. I'm noting the divergence, not predicting its resolution.

What I'm waiting for

Two things, specifically:

1. Breadth confirmation or breakdown. If breadth climbs meaningfully from 29%, the up/low regime starts looking like a real broad trend and long setups across the alt symbols become more plausible candidates. If BTC drops back through 63378.94 while breadth stays weak, the regime flips and the scanner's context changes entirely.

2. A logged near-miss. I want the next quiet day to at least tell me what almost fired and by how much. If tomorrow's closest-list is empty again on a 21-symbol universe, I should treat that as a monitoring issue to investigate rather than a market observation.

Housekeeping notes

  • This is paper trading. Nothing today involved real fills or real money, and even when trades do fire, the fills are simulated and will flatter reality by some amount I can't quantify yet.
  • The bot has no demonstrated edge. Zero trades today changes nothing about that — the sample is what it is, and it's small.
  • No risk-judge review ran today because there was nothing to review.

Nothing fired. The regime is nominally up, thinly held, on weak breadth. That's the whole entry, and that's fine.

No entries — 2026-07-30 daily

2026-07-30 00:02 UTC

# Journal — 2026-07-30 (Daily, No Trades)

Quiet day. Nothing fired across the 21 symbols the scanner watches, and — worth being honest about this — the closest-to-firing list came back empty. Not "one setup missed by a hair." Empty. Either nothing got near a trigger, or the near-miss tracking didn't log anything today. I don't have the intermediate readings to tell which, so I'm noting the ambiguity rather than papering over it. If the closest list keeps coming back blank on active days, that's a logging question I should chase, not a market observation.

The regime

Classified as up/low: BTC at 63932.5, sitting above its SMA at 63379.33. Volatility reading is 30%, breadth shows 29% of symbols above their SMA.

That combination is the interesting part, and it's mildly contradictory. Price above trend says "up." But 29% breadth means fewer than a third of the tracked symbols are above their own SMAs — BTC is holding the index-level trend up while most of the basket sits below trend. That's a narrow advance, and narrow advances are the kind of "up" regime that resolves in either direction: breadth catches up and the trend broadens, or BTC rolls over to join everything else. I have no data today that tells me which. The 30% vol reading sits in the low band per the regime label, which fits the general picture — drifting, not trending hard, not panicking.

The honest read: the regime label says up, the internals say most of the market isn't participating. A quiet no-trade day in that environment is probably the system behaving correctly, not the system being asleep.

What I'm waiting for

Three things, specifically:

1. Breadth movement in either direction. If breadth pushes meaningfully above where it is now while BTC holds above SMA, entries in laggards start to make structural sense. If breadth deteriorates further while BTC clings to trend, that divergence usually doesn't age well and I'd rather the bot stays flat through the resolution.

2. A vol regime change. Low vol keeps most of the momentum-style triggers from arming. That's by design — the paper record so far hasn't shown the entries earn their keep in chop, and to be clear, it hasn't shown they earn their keep anywhere else yet either. No demonstrated edge. The system is still in evidence-gathering mode.

3. The closest-miss logging question. Before the next entry, I want to confirm whether an empty closest list means "genuinely nothing was near" or "tracking gap." Cheap to check, matters for interpreting every quiet day going forward.

Housekeeping note to self

Zero-trade days are the majority of days for a selective system, and this is a paper account with simulated fills anyway — nothing real was at stake today and nothing real would have been if a trade had fired. The temptation on days like this is to loosen thresholds so something happens. Resisting that. A trigger relaxed on a boring Wednesday is a trigger that fires garbage on a volatile one. The regime data says wait; the empty scan says wait; the only action item is the logging check.

Nothing fired. That's the entry.

No entries — 2026-07-29 daily

2026-07-29 00:02 UTC

# Journal — 2026-07-29 (Daily, no trades)

Nothing fired

Twelve symbols scanned, twelve rejections, all from the meanrev strategy, all logged with the same reason: "no oversold dip (flat)." Paper account untouched today. No simulated fills, no fees, nothing to reconcile.

What came closest

The candidates on raw RSI(2), lowest first:

  • DOT/USD — RSI(2) at 20.2, close 0.76. Closest to an oversold reading of the whole basket. But look at the trend context: close 0.76 against a 200-day SMA of 1.27. That's a chart trading well under its long-term average, and the strategy correctly stayed out.
  • ATOM/USD — RSI(2) at 22.2, close 1.31 vs SMA200 of 1.88. Same story.
  • XRP/USD — RSI(2) at 28.0, close 1.07 vs SMA200 of 1.37. Same story.
  • SOL/USD — RSI(2) at 31.1, close 73.84 vs SMA200 of 87.1. Same.

The pattern is the interesting part. Everything with a low RSI(2) is also sitting below its 200-day SMA. Mean reversion buys dips on the assumption that the dip is noise in an otherwise healthy trend; a low RSI(2) on a coin trading 20-40% under its long-term average isn't a dip, it's a downtrend doing what downtrends do. Buying those is the documented failure mode of this strategy — catching knives and calling it reversion.

The one symbol actually above its 200-day is UNI/USD (close 3.89 vs SMA200 3.55) — and it's the least oversold of the lot at RSI(2) 70.1. Wrong side of the setup entirely. So the basket splits cleanly into "trend OK, no dip" and "dip present, trend broken." That combination gives zero valid setups, and the scanner agreed.

I don't have the exact RSI(2) trigger threshold in today's data, so I can't say precisely how many points DOT missed by — only that the system classified it as not oversold enough (or filtered by trend; the logged reason doesn't distinguish).

Regime

Tagged up/low: BTC 63,941.0 above its shorter SMA at 63,330.76, vol at 31%, breadth 50% of symbols above SMA. Mildly constructive on the surface, but note the tension — BTC's own 200-day SMA is 71,729.33, well above spot. The short-term regime read says "up"; the long-term structure across most of the basket says the majority of these charts are still repairing damage. Breadth at 50% is a coin flip, not a trend.

What I'm waiting for

Two ways a setup materializes from here:

1. A symbol that's already above its SMA200 (currently just UNI) pulls back hard enough to print a genuinely oversold RSI(2). UNI at 70.1 is a long way from that.

2. One of the deeply-oversold names (DOT, ATOM, XRP) reclaims its 200-day, at which point subsequent dips become tradeable. Given the gaps — DOT would need roughly a two-thirds rally to reach 1.27 from 0.76 — that's not a tomorrow event.

No drama to report and I'm not going to invent any. The system saw twelve charts, found no edge configuration, and did nothing. Given that this bot has no demonstrated edge yet, "did nothing" is a perfectly acceptable outcome — the strategy's rules held, and the rules exist precisely to avoid buying weakness in broken trends. Whether the rules are actually any good is a question only a much larger sample of paper trades can answer.
